name: set-active-deleted-pod
criteria: C1: After a successful `deletePod` of Pod X, while another Pod Y is active, `setActivePod(X)` leaves `getState().activePodId` equal to Y. A new test in `src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts` asserts this and is shown red against the unguarded store (red step).

C2: `setActivePod(X)` for a Pod X that `deletePod` removed issues no `lanes.list` and no `events.read` call. A new test asserts the fake API's call counts for X stay unchanged across the call, and it is shown red against the unguarded store (red step).

C3: Only tombstoned ids are refused. An id the store has never seen still becomes `activePodId` (the existing `'ghost'` test at `src/renderer/src/state/workspace-provider.test.tsx:1004` passes unchanged), and a Pod whose `pods.delete` call failed can still be activated, which a new test asserts. `setActivePod(null)` behaves as before.
C4: The `setActivePod` docblock in `store.ts` states the deleted-Pod rule in place and cites no `.sir/sessions` path or session id.
C5: `npm test` (whole suite, run from the repository root) passes, and `npm run typecheck` exits 0.

C6: Row 43 of `.sir/backlog.md` (2026-11-16 20261116-1932-deleted-pod-runtime-guard, '`setActivePod` can still make a deleted Pod's id the `activePodId`') is removed at Gate 3, and every open backlog row citing a `file:line` in a file this session changes is re-measured at the tip.
